evidence_quotes.quote: Ultimately, the DAUSRs were estimated for 154 countries.
The results indicated that despite improvements in rural sanitation, 12.2% of rural populations will still lack access to sanitary toilets
in 2030, with an estimated 243,000 deaths (CI: 147,000−441,000) due to unsafe rural sanitation environments.
highlights the need for better rural sanitation governance to provide for demographic shifts, such as aging and declining fertility rates,

country.comment: The study estimates rural sanitation conditions and Deaths Attributable to Unsafe Sanitation in Rural areas (DAUSRs) globally across 154 countries, grouped both into six geographical regions (Africa, Mediterranean/Eastern Mediterranean, Europe, Americas, Southeast Asia, Western Pacific) and four World Bank/WHO income tiers.
country.where_found: PDF p. 2, Section 2.1; PDF p. 3, Section 2.2

effect_estimate.comment: No quantitative effect estimate is reported for any legal, regulatory, or governance variable (governance is discussed only as a policy implication). Note that on PDF p. 7 (Section 3.3), one sentence prints '59.5 million' for improved sanitation facilities (2020-2030) while the immediately following sentence states '59.5 thousand deaths' consistent with Figure 4.
effect_estimate.value: No numeric effect estimate for a legal/governance variable (sanitation governance is inferred only). Across N = 154 countries (2000–2030), global rural sanitation coverage for 'Improved Settings' and 'Safely Managed' increased by 11.9% (to 64.8% in 2030) and 6.45% (to 23.0% in 2030), respectively, while 'Unimproved & Untreated Settings' decreased by 18.4%, leaving 12.2% of rural populations without sanitary toilets in 2030. Annual global DAUSRs and age-standardized mortality rates are projected to fall from 2000 to 2030 by 816.7 thousand deaths and 25.2 per 100,000, respectively, to 243,000 deaths (95% CI: 147,000–441,000) in 2030; improvements in rural sanitary conditions contributed a reduction of 59.5 thousand deaths in 2020–2030, while rural aging (+480 thousand deaths) and population growth (+56.8 thousand deaths) increased DAUSRs over 2000–2030.

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: The study is a macro-epidemiological global burden-of-disease modeling, time-series forecasting (BAPC and ARIMA), and decomposition simulation study based on aggregate GBD 2021 and WHO secondary estimates (2000–2030), rather than a randomized trial, quasi-experimental policy evaluation, primary cross-sectional survey, individual cohort study, qualitative study, systematic review, or doctrinal legal study.

sample_size.comment: Screened from 204 countries in GBD 2021 (2000–2020) and 170 countries in the WHO rural sanitation dataset (2000–2021) after excluding countries with missing or outlier data, yielding 154 countries modeled from 2000 to 2030. No individual or household sample size is reported.
sample_size.value: 154 countries (modeled from 2000 to 2030, using historical GBD 2021 data for 2000–2020 from 204 countries and WHO rural sanitation data for 2000–2021 from 170 countries, plus projections for 2021–2030)
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 2, Section 2.1; PDF pp. 2–3, Section 2.2 & Table 1

study_design.comment: Integrates GBD 2021 epidemiological relative risks/mortality data and WHO rural sanitation coverage data to estimate historical DAUSRs (2000–2020), forecast sanitation coverage and mortality to 2030 via ARIMA and Bayesian MCMC age-period-cohort models, and decompose changes across five demographic, sanitation, and mortality drivers.
study_design.value: Global macro-epidemiological modeling, time-series forecasting, and decomposition study integrating Comparable Risk Assessment (CRA), Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) models, and AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) models using secondary GBD and WHO country-level data (2000–2030)
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 2–4, Sections 2.1–2.4 & Figure 1
